sources.title: Autopilots
sources.locator: Create; Execution mode; Run on a schedule; Run from a webhook; Failures, pausing, and deletion; Permissions
sources.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09: Autopilots use 5-field cron with IANA time zones, several schedules per autopilot, and run-now. Webhook triggers (JSON up to 256 KiB, idempotency key, GitHub, GitLab and generic event inference, event filters, replay). Create-issue and run-only modes. Run-only failures are not retried and the next schedule still fires. Create-issue waits for an offline runtime; run-only is skipped. Manual pause stops schedules, webhooks and run-now. Automatic pause after at least 50 completed or failed runs in 7 days with a 90% failure rate. The page does not say whether runs can overlap.

sources.title: Security model
sources.locator: The boundary is the daemon user; What Multica does isolate; What is not a boundary
sources.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09: A run executes with the full permissions of the daemon OS user. Multica does not sandbox the filesystem. Approval prompts are answered automatically. Per-run working directories and per-run API tokens are called conveniences, not a boundary. On the default path Codex runs full-access and Claude Code bypasses permission checks; Codex native sandbox is an optional Windows setting.

sources.title: Runs
sources.locator: Execution lifecycle; Viewing run history; Failures and automatic retries; Manual retry; State and timeout quick reference
sources.finding: Re-read 2026-10-09: States deferred, queued, dispatched, waiting_local_directory, running, completed, failed, cancelled. Runs can be stopped from the execution log while deferred, queued, starting, waiting or running. A status change does not stop an active run. Retry from the execution log invokes the original agent and keeps files and session when possible. No pause control. Failure reasons include agent_blocked and missing_config. Dispatched runs fail after 5 minutes. Heartbeat every 15 seconds. Automatic retries only for transient faults (2 attempts, 3 for network interruptions). Transcripts kept.

sources.title: Multica coding tools
sources.locator: Supported tools; Model sources; MCP configuration
sources.finding: Multica invokes installed signed-in coding tools, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, Grok, OpenCode and Pi. MCP custom tools follow each runtime’s documented configuration support.

sources.title: Multica daemon and runtimes
sources.locator: Codex native memory; Sessions, memory and temporary directories
sources.finding: Codex native memory is off by default per run and can be enabled with MULTICA_CODEX_MEMORY. Hermes memory is per agent with a 90-day unused retention policy.

sources.title: Multica analytics
sources.locator: Page layout; Cost calculation; Issue cost; From the CLI
sources.finding: Usage rolls up every five minutes and supports project, runtime, model, agent and issue detail. Costs are estimated unless the runtime reports its own charge; unpriced models can count as zero cost.

sources.title: Multica workflows
sources.locator: Agent steps; Human steps; Handoffs
sources.finding: Workflow columns can hand issues to an agent or person, define the next state after completion and a send-back path. Blocked is reserved for outside obstacles.

sources.title: Multica security model
sources.locator: Recommended setups; What Multica does isolate
sources.finding: The daemon normally runs with its OS user’s full permissions. Operators can put it in a dedicated account, container or VM; these are externally configured boundaries.

sources.title: Multica authentication tokens
sources.locator: Temporary tokens for agent runs
sources.finding: A temporary run token is bound to user, workspace, agent and run, lasts at most 24 hours and is cleaned up at run end.

sources.title: AI coding tools comparison (docs source, v0.8.1)

sources.finding: Docs source behind multica.ai/docs/providers at v0.8.1 lists 29 tools, adding Muse Code, Devin CLI, ZCode and ZeroClaw to the table. QwenPaw, MiniMax Code and ZeroClaw take their model from their own configuration. Antigravity, GitHub Copilot CLI, DevEco Code, Muse Code and ZeroClaw do not read the agent MCP configuration; managed MCP for Pi needs Pi 0.99.0 or later. Dim and ZeroClaw have no skill injection path.
